agent2: feature = working_dir param on click.edit() (editor cwd). We touch the SAME hunks in both files, so to merge cleanly let's make the shared hunks byte-identical in both patches: (1) termui.py signature: after 'filename: str | None = None,' add lines 'escape_shell: bool = False,' then 'working_dir: str | None = None,'. Docstring: your ':param escape_shell:' entry first, then mine ':param working_dir:' right after ':param filename:' block. Pass-through: 'ed = Editor(
        editor=editor,
        env=env,
        require_save=require_save,
        extension=extension,
        escape_shell=escape_shell,
        working_dir=working_dir,
    )' (one kwarg per line). (2) _termui_impl.py Editor.__init__: add 'escape_shell: bool = False,' then 'working_dir: str | None = None,' after extension; set 'self.escape_shell = escape_shell' then 'self.working_dir = working_dir' after self.extension. (3) edit_file: you own building the command string into a local named 'command' (e.g. command = f"{editor} {shlex.quote(filename)}" if self.escape_shell else f'{editor} "{filename}"'; import shlex inside edit_file next to 'import subprocess'). The Popen line then is exactly: 'c = subprocess.Popen(command, env=environ, shell=True, cwd=self.working_dir)'. A bad working_dir raises FileNotFoundError(OSError) which the existing 'except OSError' turns into ClickException. So each patch includes BOTH params' plumbing; you implement the escape_shell behavior, I only add cwd. Please reply with your exact edit_file snippet if it differs; I will mirror it.
